title: Macrophage Dysfunction in Atherosclerosis and Cardiometabolic Diseases
text:
Atherosclerosis, obesity and non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) mediate increased risk for cardiovascular
disease. This Program Project will probe the effects of caloric restriction, LXRα phosphorylation, Netrin1 and its
receptor network and RAGE/DIAPH1 in these pathologies. The Program Project will discover mediating
mechanisms and identify therapeutic targets for, ultimately, clinical trials in human patients.

title: Dual function for an effector immunity protein in Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm biogenesis
text:
Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Pa) forms robust biofilms, aggregates of bacteria encased in a protective
extracellular matrix, in the airways of people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) and is a major cause of morbidity and
mortality for pwCF. This application proposes that TsiT, a type VI secretion system (T6SS) immunity protein
which is highly conserved across Gram-negative bacterial pathogens, has a secondary function as a
transcription factor that regulates biofilm. The project will serve as a foundation for the candidate to develop
skills as an academic researcher and provide far reaching insights into biofilm regulation and thus clinical
treatment.

title: HPV, HIV and Oral Microbiota Interplay in Nigerian Youth (HOMINY)
text:
Perinatal exposure to and infection with HIV disrupts both the oral immune system and the microbes that normally
inhabit the mouth (including the bacterial microbiome), increasing the risk of oral HPV and resulting cancers, yet
this risk has never been characterized in youth. Using a large cohort of children born to HIV-infected mothers
(alongside a comparison group born to uninfected mothers), this study seeks to understand the risk of oral HPV,
and how the oral microbiome shapes oral HPV persistence in youth perinatally exposed to or/and infected with
HIV. Study findings will ultimately provide a comprehensive evidence base needed to guide future US-based
HPV-vaccination, screening, and prevention strategies for oropharyngeal cancer, which has now surpassed
cervical cancer as the most common HPV-associated cancer in the US.

title: Colonic epithelial wound healing by anal transitional cells
text:
Inflammatory bowel disease represents a collection of medically incurable illnesses that cause severe and
chronic damage to the lining of the bowel. Although all available therapies for IBD target the overactive
immune system, promotion of healing of the damaged bowel through regenerative medicine represents a
promising complementary strategy. Here, we elucidate important aspects of a noncanonical colonic wound
healing response that originates from the neighboring skin-like anal transition zone and which could yield
therapeutic insights.

title: Mechanistic Investigation of RNA-Mediated Gene Regulation and Immunity
text:
The proposed synthetic biology effort will lead to the development of novel genome editing applications. The
described high-resolution mechanistic studies of CRISPR interference system in prokaryotes will not only
contribute to the development of strategies to control microbial pathogens, but also inspire the development of
new genome editing tools.

title: Membrane remodeling by membrane-bound motor
text:
Defects in cytoskeletal-membrane coupling underlie many human diseases, including cancer metastasis,
neurodegeneration, immune disorders, kidney diseases, and deafness. This project will uncover how membrane-
bound myosin-I motors coordinate actin dynamics and membrane remodeling to shape cells. Understanding
these fundamental mechanisms will reveal new principles of cell morphogenesis and identify potential strategies
for diagnosing and treating cytoskeletal and membrane-associated diseases.

title: SCH: Artificial Intelligence enabled multi-modal sensor platform for at-home health monitoring of patients
text:
Our proposed research is highly relevant to NIBIB mission to transform through engineering the 
understanding of disease and its prevention, detection, diagnosis, and treatment. Our research goal is to 
develop AI-enabled MUSE technology for at-home health monitoring of AKI patients through fusion of urine 
biomarkers, ECG and EMR. Our research aligns perfectly with Goals 2 and 4 of NIBIB Strategic Vision by 
making healthcare more accessible to all through development of point-of-care wireless and personal health 
informatics technology. Our work will lead to new insights into health management of AKI patients.

title: A novel approach of age-grading of mosquitoes using SERS and machine learning models
text:
Only older mosquitoes are competent to transmit pathogens to humans. This project is aimed to develop a
rapid, accurate, and robust approach to determine the age of mosquitoes in the field which is critically needed
to assess health risks associated with vector-borne diseases. Having the ability to detect vector age in the field
would also enable rapid assessment of control strategies, especially those designed to manage or minimize
insecticide resistance development.

title: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Imaging Core
text: Core G: Imaging PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT The imaging data set collected in the Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) participants to date represents a highly valuable resource for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) research. It has supported cross sectional and longitudinal analyses of PET and MRI data to develop a timeline for imaging biomarkers in autosomal dominant AD (ADAD). With this application, the DIAN Imaging Core will continue to obtain and analyze longitudinal imaging data that is fully integrated with clinical, psychometric, genetic and fluid biomarkers, and will allow for mutation-specific genotype-phenotype analysis. Imaging Core will be responsible for the acquisition, quality control, and analysis of the MRI and PET neuroimaging for DIAN. Carriers of AD-causing mutations and their non-carrier siblings are enrolled and followed in the Clinical Core through the international DIAN performance sites. Participants will undergo structural and functional MRI, amyloid PET and tau PET in conjunction with their clinical visits. The source imaging data and post-processed data will be available to collaborating and outside investigators and will be distributed by the Biostatistics Core. Based on our prior crossover study, we will allow sites to choose between amyloid PET with [11C]-Pittsburgh Compound B (PiB) or [18F]-Florbetapir (FBP), in order to reduce burden on participants and costs for the study. For tau PET, we will continue to obtain scans with the tracers [18F]-MK-6240, [18F]-Flortaucipir (FTP). Because no single tracer has the international distribution to reach all sites, each site is assigned one for the three tau PET tracers. Using multiple tracers maximizes the number of DIAN sites that can perform tau PET imaging. Including multiple tracers across the study diminishes the risk of choosing one tracer for such a large, international study of unique participants. We recognize the limitations of using multiple tracers in the same study and have taken steps to minimize this risk. DIAN Imaging Core leaders are involved with multisite studies focused on optimizing standardization procedures for tau PET tracers which will greatly benefit this study. Over the course of the proposal we will also work with pharma partners to strengthen tracer availability throughout the network.

title: Advancing Cancer Research Through Next Generation Sequencing at Mays Cancer Center of UT Health San Antonio
text:
This R50 application seeks fund to support Dr. Zhao Lai, Director of the Next-Generation Sequencing Shared
Resource (NGSSR) of the NCI-designated Mays Cancer Center at the University of Texas Health San Antonio.
The NGSSR, heavily used by Cancer Center members and investigators in the San Antonio area, has a strong
focus on its unique Hispanic population, and provides cutting-edge high throughput sequencing expertise and
analytical capacities to support diverse genomic applications. Dr. Lai, a highly skilled and well-trained genomics
scientist, is a critical member who leads a cutting-edge scientific team in the NGSSR that supports and
contributes intellectually to many NCI-funded projects through its expert genomic analyses.

title: Exploring the structural space underlying antibody-mediated Fc-effector functions
text:
Antibodies play a major role in shaping infectious disease and cancer outcomes by mediating Fc-effector
functions, yet the molecular basis of Fc potency remains unclear. Our cryoET/cryoEM approach is expected to
uncover novel structural features that will translate into testable hypotheses for structural correlates of Fc effector
functions. This knowledge can be applied in general to develop antibody therapeutics and inform the design of
immunogens to elicit potent Fc-effector functions.

title: Assembling the Genetic Architecture of X-linked Dystonia Parkinsonism
text:
We previously discovered that a large insertion in intron 32 of TAF1 is functionally associated with intron retention
and alternative splicing in the disease X-linked dystonia parkinsonism (XDP) and that there are protein
aggregates in XDP postmortem brain. In this renewal, we will determine whether these signatures can be
ameliorated by treating with antisense oligonucleotides, including if the treatment has an impact on the clearance
of protein aggregates from cultures of neurons and glia. This endeavor will clarify the disease mechanism and
inform future genetic therapy for XDP and many other neurodegenerative diseases with which XDP has
commonalities, such as Alzheimer’s Disease, Parkinson’s Disease, and Huntington’s Disease.

title: CRISPR detection of circulating cell-free Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) DNA for rapid diagnosis and monitoring of MAC pulmonary disease
text:
Chronic Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) pulmonary disease is an increasingly common orphan disease
that causes progressive disability in older adults and has a tremendous unmet therapeutic need. We seek to
conduct analytic and clinical validation of a CRISPR-based blood test for MAC cell-free DNA as a measure of
MAC pulmonary disease activity and treatment response. This biomarker could ultimately be used to guide
diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making with regard to MAC pulmonary disease.

title: Mapping the human DRG and spinal cord functional genome at cellular and spatial resolution
text: There are clear differences between mouse and human nociceptors that have profound implications for the development of pain therapeutics that target the peripheral nervous system. Our spatial sequencing experiments reveal a distinct set of cell types in the human dorsal root ganglion (DRG). In this research project, we will compare DRG tissues from organ donors and surgical patients with chronic pain. We will include a range of ages across the adult life-span in both men and women in an ethnically diverse population. In addition to the DRG, we will also examine the spinal cord. We have already conducted SPLiT-seq and spatial transcriptomic analysis of dorsal and ventral horn from a select number of organ donors demonstrating the viability of both techniques. Our data shows that like the DRG, there are clear species differences in the spinal cord highlighting the importance of this discovery work. In our first aim we will use spatial sequencing and SPLiT-seq technologies to precisely define the cell types of the human DRG. We will use organ donor and pain patient DRGs to define how cellular transcriptomes change with pain, and if the changes covary with sex and age. SN ATAC-seq will identify transcriptional states and regulatory elements in human DRG. In our second aim we will use the same technologies to map the cell types of the human dorsal horn. We will strive to use the combined DRG and spinal cord data to understand how DRG neuron subtypes are likely to connect to subsets of dorsal horn neurons. We will fully characterize the human neurons that comprise the spino-thalamic tract. Finally, in our third aim we will use ribosome profiling on human DRG and spinal cord to gain new insight into translational events in these tissues. Long-read sequencing will be used to map RNA modifications and splicing in a set of mRNAs that are critical for pain. Our work will create a comprehensive atlas of the transcriptome, epi-transcriptome, and translatome of neurons that comprise the first synapses in the pain pathway, including in chronic pain conditions.

title: Expanding Swabseq sequencing technology to enable readiness for emerging pathogens
text: The research proposed here extends on our previous research to develop scalable, rapid mass screening approaches for testing of SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. Extending on genomic technologies, we will expand our sequencing-based approach to emerging pathogens such as monkey pox and Polio, develop agnostic testing approaches to rapidly screen for COVID19. This technology can inform public health measures lo rapidly identify outbreaks and control the spread of infection and can encompass both diagnosis and viral variant detection simultaneously.

title: Characterization of novel pyrazole compounds with potent anti-cancer activity
text:
We recently discovered two similar anti-cancer compounds with potent toxic activity
against many types of human cancer cells. In this proposal, we will perform the requisite
experiments to determine how the compounds cause death and if they are able to kill
human cancers growing in mice. We expect that in the near future, the identified anti-
cancer drugs will result in therapeutic agents that can be used alone or in combination
with other FDA approved drugs for the treatment of human cancer and help reduce
cancer health disparities.

title: Exploring the Interface between Substance Use Disorders and other Forms of Psychopathology using Phenotypic and Genomic Approaches
text:
The interface between substance use, externalizing, and internalizing disorders is complex and poorly
characterized, which limits efforts to identify causes, correlates, and treatments for substance use disorders
(SUDs). The training and research described in this proposal will integrate phenotypic classification of SUDs
with statistical genetics and translational science to better characterize the phenotypic and genetic
relationships among SUDs and other forms of psychopathology. This project has the potential to improve the
specificity of phenotypes used in future studies, aid in gene discovery of SUDs, and improve the clinical utility
of classification and gene-identification efforts for SUDs.

title: Preclinical Development of First-in-Class NDUFS7 Antagonists for the Treatment of Pancreatic Cancer
text:
The proposed studies are relevant to public health because discovery of novel drugs to treat pancreatic cancer
represents a significant unmet need in oncology. This work is thus relevant to NIH’s mission to develop impactful
new treatment for pancreatic cancer, a disease with no cure.

title: Multidisciplinary Implementation Research for malaria control and elimination in West Africa
text:
Sub-Saharan Africa region continues to bear the brunt of the global malaria burden despite wide deployment of
control interventions. This multidisciplinary program will contribute to improve our understanding of the changing
malaria epidemiology and transmission in relation with control interventions. We will developpe, evaluate and
optimize ongoing malaria control strategies to produce maximum impact on transmission interruption and
elimination through implementation research. We will characterize critical barriers related to changing
epidemiological patterns, drug and insecticide resistance to develop adaptive evidence-based interventions to
meet the evolving needs of control programs.

title: Effect of hippocampal feedback projections on the function of the early olfactory system
text:
The proposed research will investigate the role of vCA1 feedback on neural representations of environment
and odors in the main olfactory bulb, a circuit critical to sensory perception and memory. Mice are one of the
major model organisms for studying olfaction, and many circuits principles are conserved across evolution,
making them critical to understanding neurodegenerative and neurological disorders like Alzheimer’s Disease,
Parkinson’s and COVID. This proposal will improve our understanding of the functional coupling between brain
regions involved in sensory perception and those involved in learning, emotion, and memory.
